method_limits: 'left the tree' is E523's name for a second-hop callee outside the corpus; this study re-reads the receiving call on its own line, so a `sys.exit(main())` entry point is published as the process exit, not as a library boundary
a value stored into a container is published as an unfollowed form, never as a reader this scan reached
the boundary is named from the cited source line only; a line that does not parse is published as an unresolved name with that evidence, not assumed
the two upstream classes stay separate in every tally: a left-the-tree row and a still-forwarded row are never added into one 'residue resolved' number

several rows can share one physical second-hop parcel (one function's return arm read by several first readers); the parcel tallies are de-duplicated on (source, line, callee) and every parcel publishes rows_that_share_this_parcel
nothing is executed and no source is rewritten
sources_read and the parcel count are a snapshot of a live tree that other lanes write to; they are published but not gated, while every boundary class is re-derived
